title: Adaptive Tuner - Guided Recommendation Flow (Draft)
content:
Purpose
This doc captures a lightweight, task-oriented wireframe and interaction notes for a guided "tuner" that surfaces prescriptive recommendations across batching, caching, and quantization. Intended as a design + engineering volley: product team demo -> eng feasibility -> small UX iteration -> experiment. Focus: fast discoverability, actionable deltas, and safe rollback.

Problem statement
- Customers want prescriptive guidance to reduce per-token cost while keeping latency and quality within acceptable bounds.
- Current Optimize recs are many discrete suggestions; users tell us they aren’t sure how to sequence them or what tradeoffs to expect.
- Need a low-friction flow that: 1) assesses current config, 2) presents a prioritized small set of changes, 3) previews economic and latency impact, and 4) applies changes with a canary and rollback plan.

High-level concept
- 'Adaptive Tuner' is a guided modal/side-panel that walks the user through 3 steps: Audit -> Prescribe -> Validate.
- Each step is scaffolded with inline data and a recommended default for quick apply, plus an "advanced" view for manual tuning.

Wireframe notes (screen order)
1) Trigger: Per-model toolbar button labeled 'Tune' (tooltip: Guided cost/latency suggestions). Clicking opens the Tuner side-panel.
2) Audit view (collapsed top): quick snapshot of current SLOs, avg latency p50/p95, tokens / minute, recent cold-starts, baseline throughput. Inline short explanation for any unusual metrics (hover help).
3) Prescribe list (center): a ranked list of candidate prescriptions. Each card shows: title (e.g., "Use prefix/KV caching for 3 common prompts"), short rationale, projected delta (cost %, latency change ms), confidence band (Low/Med/High), primary risk (e.g., quality delta), and action buttons: Preview | Apply canary | Save as preset.
   - Card variants: Batching, Caching, Quantization. Cards may be combined into a single "apply bundle" when dependencies exist.
4) Preview differences (panel): side-by-side token-level cost calc, trace of expected latency change across typical sequence lengths, sample inference outputs for a trimmed set of prompts (diff heatmap).
5) Canary apply flow: lightweight modal to pick traffic percentage (1%, 5%, 20%), duration, and fallback policy (auto-rollback threshold on quality or latency). Include quick simulation of expected cost during canary.
6) Monitoring & validation (post-apply): in the Tuner panel show real-time canary metrics, quality regressions flagged by eval set, and an explicit 'Promote' button after canary succeeds.

Microcopy and UI copy examples
- Prescribe card header: "Enable KV cache on session-start (expected -12% cost, +3ms latency)"
- Confidence label: "Confidence: Medium — based on 18 runs on similar workloads"
- Preview CTA: "Run preview (3 sample prompts)"
- Canary CTA: "Run canary at 5% traffic for 4h"
- Fallback hint: "Auto-rollback if p95 > baseline + 30ms or eval loss increase > 0.5%"

Interaction details and edge cases
- Dependency grouping: If quantization lowers model size and batching affects memory residency, show a dependency warning and an ordered apply sequence suggestion.
- Permission gating: Only orgs with edit privileges on the model config may Apply; others see 'Propose changes' to generate a change request.
- Fail-safe: Any 'Apply' action creates a named change-set with immutable diff and an auto-rollback TTL.
- Offline preview: If preview infrastructure busy, fall back to a simulated preview using previously captured traces and model profilers. Mark simulated previews clearly.

Acceptance criteria (MVP)
- User can open Tuner from model detail and see Audit + Prescribe list for that model.
- Each prescription card contains projected cost delta and a confidence label.
- Preview runs at least 3 prompts and shows side-by-side token/cost comparison.
- User can apply a canary (choose traffic % and duration), and the system will record the change-set and start metric collection.
- Canary page shows p50/p95, error rate, and eval-set quality measure; auto-rollback triggers if thresholds breached.

Telemetry and instrumentation
- Events: tuner.open, tuner.preview.start, tuner.preview.finish, tuner.apply.canary, tuner.canary.promote, tuner.canary.rollback, tuner.save.preset.
- Attributes: model_id, preset_id, user_id, canary_pct, canary_duration_hours, delta_cost_percent, delta_p95_ms, apply_mode (manual|auto), preview_mode (real|simulated).

Backlog and engineering notes
- Backlog items (priority):
  1) Backend: estimator endpoint to return cost/latency deltas for a proposed change-set (JIRA-824 linked).
  2) Frontend: side-panel skeleton + card component library + preview diff UI (component PR referenced).
  3) Canary engine: small API to create change-sets and attach auto-rollback rules.
  4) Preset store: allow users to save bundles and tag them (team/purpose).
  5) Accessibility pass: keyboard navigation and screen reader labels for the Tuner.

Rollout plan
- Internal alpha: product + infra (2 weeks) using a small set of internal models.
- Beta: opt-in for customers with >=100k tokens/day, monitoring feature flags and SLOs.
- Gradual public launch: gate by region and dedicated vs hosted customers. Track unit economics.

Open questions (to resolve in grooming)
- What is the canonical eval set for canaries? Per-customer custom eval or shared baseline?
- How to quantify "confidence" precisely — past-run counts vs distributional similarity metric?
- Should we allow multi-prescription "bundles" to be suggested automatically or keep suggestions single-change-first?
- UX: inline vs modal previews — which disrupts current console workflows least?

Next steps for this doc
- Sync with infra (Samir) to validate estimator latency and feasibility.
- Engineering spike to implement a minimal estimator that returns delta cost and p95 delta for small changes. (owner: Marcus, ETA: 2 weeks)
- Design mockups for the side-panel in Figma (Leila to iterate 2 variants: compact and detailed).

Appendix: quick sketch annotations
- Sketch A: Compact view shows 2 top cards and an "Apply Quick" button that applies best-effort bundle at 5% canary.
- Sketch B: Detailed view opens preview drawer with prompt diff heatmap and toggle for simulated=true/false.
- Notes on copy tone: keep language pragmatic and ops-focused—avoid marketing-speak.

If you're reviewing: leave inline comments on the Prescribe card fields, and flag any backend assumptions that are unrealistic.
